subject.title: Feature Request: Add Edge TTS support

question: Should Windows Voice Mode reuse OpenClaw's existing gateway-level Microsoft TTS provider, or own a separate node-local Edge TTS integration?
rationale: Both approaches can provide the requested voices, but they establish different long-term provider contracts, privacy disclosures, dependency boundaries, and failure behavior; repository history does not establish which layer should own this duplication.

options.title: Reuse Gateway Provider
options.body: Route compatible Voice Mode synthesis through OpenClaw's existing Microsoft TTS provider and avoid maintaining a second Edge protocol implementation.

options.title: Add Node Provider
options.body: Approve a node-local catalog provider when offline-independent Windows playback is required, with explicit egress disclosure and end-to-end proof.

options.title: Decline Bundling
options.body: Keep the current provider set and leave unsupported Edge integration outside the bundled Windows node.

recommendation.title: Reuse Gateway Provider
recommendation.body: Route compatible Voice Mode synthesis through OpenClaw's existing Microsoft TTS provider and avoid maintaining a second Edge protocol implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: RBrid introduced the shared TTS capability contract and has the strongest history connection to deciding where another provider belongs.
